newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait still wants to privatise telecommunications.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait still wants to privatise telecommunications.

text.p: Kuwait still wants to privatise its telecommunications services, a communications ministry official said in remarks published on Monday.
"There is an inclination to turn the Communications Ministry into a Kuwaiti telecommunications company," al-Seyassah newspaper quoted undersecretary Waleed al-Najar as saying.
"A bill in this respect has been sent by the cabinet to parliament and we are optimistic that it will come out at any time," he added.

In 1992, the government sent to parliament a measure allowing for the creation of a shareholder firm that will take over the telecommunications services, laying out the legal framework for privatising the services.

MPs have said they sought rules to govern privatisations before any such move can be allowed, citing concern about layoffs and charge increases by the private sector on services currently provided by the state at subsidised rates.
"The (envisaged) telecommunications firm will be a profit-making institution not a losing firm," said the official.
"The firm will be a shareholding company in which the government will have a stake...and there is a possibility for also having a foreign partner."
Since 1994 Kuwait has sold its stake in some 18 local firms for over $2 billion in the first phase of a privatisation plan, while 36 more worth some $3 billion still remain, officials say.
The government hopes to get parliament's approval in 1997 to start the more controversial stage of privatising public utilities such as water, electricity and telecommunications.
